researchNotes: Original authors preserved. Reconciled stale local IDs against live title, source and author before mutation, with immediate pre-write identity checks and full backups. No unrelated application edits.

Read fresh MISO and SPP queue records, the August 2026 EIA workbook, CAISO queue and NYISO workbook. Queue MW and requested service dates do not establish ownership, construction or actual operation. EIA reporting coordinates and address geocodes are approximate context, not surveyed boundaries.

Cleared 17 unsupported capital costs and five calculated energy rows in each environment. Removed fabricated developer attribution, four-hour battery MWh assumptions and unsupported grid voltages. The 5C Phoenix waiver does not substantiate a native power or datacenter rating; those rows were removed.

DEN2 is 4 MW IT / 31,510 IT sqft; the 20 MW figure covers DEN2 plus DEN5. Its event is the confirmed February 2, 2022 property acquisition. MSP3 is Brooklyn Park, 9 MW critical / 82,231 IT sqft, not Maple Plain. Its 2021 opening is represented by an estimated year placeholder.

DC BLOX current brochure distinguishes BHM1-B 40 MW critical / 60 MW gross and 263,000 sqft, versus a separate 54 MW initial move-in entry for March 2027 whose basis remains unclear. The 2024 URL serves updated brochure contents. Existing-campus photographs do not establish expansion completion. The downloaded community overview does not contain the expansion wording shown in one search snippet; the opened brochure controls.

HostDime SuperNova is 100,000 sqft / seven stories / three datacenter floors at 1 Innovative Place. The press kit distinguishes 12 MW electrical from 6 MW Tier IV redundant capacity. Current operator wording describes final construction and commissioning preparation ahead of opening; no opening date inferred. The event is the estimated December 2020 groundbreaking month.

Mammoth Central I is a separate 300 MW EIA unit from Central II. The October 7, 2026 company celebration covers the remaining 900 MW program and says imminent operation, not proof of a Central-I-only COD. Conflicting EIA and generic operator schedules remain documented.

Rich Road is 240 MW in Canton. NYPA announced its 51% majority position on September 28, 2026, with late-2027 construction and 2029 operation targets. That current announcement supersedes older EIA/NYISO forecast dates; the September 24, 2024 ORES permit was downloaded and read. Rich Road is not the claimed generic Boralex Massena project.

Bouse is CAISO 2052, with 1,010.88 MW storage, 1,009.9 MW solar and 1,000 MW combined export; the component ratings are not additive export capability. DEGA pairs 200 MW solar with 200 MW battery, not 400 MW battery. Centralia CENT bn LLC is separate from unsupported joint ownership assertions. Sebastian GEN2022-130 is 200 MW; a separate 50 MW request is not added to it.

Gibson EIA 68455 reports operation in August 2025; Old Hayneville EIA 68001 reports August 2026. Month placeholders remain estimated rather than claiming an exact day. White Tank is EIA 70033, 100 MW with March 2027 target. Lawrence County is TVA EIA 67233, 193 MW with December 2027 target and approvals not initiated.

Hillsboro III current operator is Panthera Grid Partners, formerly Urban Grid, with 200 MW under construction and early-2027 target. The operator/EIA status and date conflict is explicit. Existing Mammoth (pin 16317), Hillsboro and Sebastian overlaps are queued for identity review; no automatic merge or synthetic source URL fragments.

Fourteen coordinate corrections required 42 replacement USGS maps. DEN2, Birmingham and 5C use Census address geocodes; MSP3 uses a matched ArcGIS PointAddress because Census did not match. HostDime uses its operator-linked Google Maps point. Other corrected locations use the cited EIA reporting coordinates. Coarse Keystone, Bouse and Sebastian context points retain their nine maps.

Official gallery and linked-photo checks yielded 20 credited assets: 13 photographs, three renderings and four diagrams. DEN2 supplies four photos; MSP3 two photos and two interior visualizations; Birmingham one existing-building photo, one expansion concept and one plan; HostDime six photos; Rich Road and Hillsboro regional diagrams; Mammoth a company ceremony photo covering South and Central I/II. Each caption identifies scope and limitations. No photographic inference of commissioning or operating capacity.

Primary source access gaps are explicit. NYPA was opened through web despite plain-client access trouble. QTS pages were opened through web where direct clients were blocked. Edwards Air Force FAQ/opportunity pages were search-indexed but direct downloads returned 403, leaving an exact awarded project unverified. Broader lease solicitation is not cancellation evidence. Official galleries for queue-only or held identities did not provide an adoptable verified project photo; unrelated Corby and other-campus images were not substituted.

Seven soft-delete holds have specific evidence gaps: Concord 200 MW identity; Ipava standalone 300 MW versus distinct queue requests; Solano storage identity versus separate Corby and wind projects; QTS Hillsboro phase-specific scope; Johnston County two competing 200 MW requests; Edwards AFB awarded project versus lease solicitation; QTS Denver DC2-specific scope versus campus totals. Held on both environments, not declared cancelled.

All 48 fresh pin/metric read-backs, 71 current Azure files and 34 retained native pages verified. Draft catalogs and both posted maps synchronized to 1,408 entries. No deployment, restart or production build. Credit balance is not exposed; stopped at a fully verified 24-pin checkpoint.
